actionable.title: Apply bounded metadata validation to the bootstrap wrapper read
actionable.problem: Both bootstrap wrappers still execute node -p with require(.../pi-agents/package.json).version and print the result before the final Python verifier calls its new bounded, typed check_packages reader. Installed package metadata is outside the approved policy inventory, and the new static preflight intentionally skips this metadata. A matching approved policy therefore does not prevent a non-version string or object from reaching the wrapper console/log, or an oversized metadata file from being read without the 1,000,000-byte limit. The final verifier rejecting that metadata cannot undo the prior output or resource consumption. This path requires neither a failed preflight nor concurrent filesystem substitution.
actionable.fix: Remove the duplicate raw Node metadata read and rely on the final verifier, or expose a shared safe metadata reader that enforces regular-file, bounded-read, object-root and version-string validation before any wrapper output. Add wrapper-level synthetic coverage for a non-version marker and oversized metadata, preserving the existing preflight ordering.
actionable.reproduction: Source-traced; no new dynamic probe was executed because this review was limited to existing harmless tests. In an otherwise valid synthetic fixture with a matching policy baseline, put {"version":"SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_MARKER"} in the installed pi-agents/package.json. Wrapper step 5 forwards that value from Node to its output before the final verifier rejects the version and records installed=null. A JSON metadata file above MAX_PACKAGE_MANIFEST_BYTES reaches the same unbounded Node require call. Existing test_invalid_installed_metadata_returns_failure_receipt_without_copying_content and test_package_metadata_read_is_bounded exercise only the Python reader; wrapper tests replace Node with a shim that never reads package.json.
